title: Using natural cognition to translate across species
summary: A staggering 96% of all neuropsychiatric clinical trials fail. An important reason for this is that research is not translatable between species; changes in behaviour as a result of neurological or psychiatric conditions are often difficult to reproduce in animals. This is due mainly to the tradition of studying the brain in a very unnatural way, and studying the same thought processes very differently across animals. Here, we record brain activity from healthy participants engaged in natural behaviour in a virtual reality setting, and compare this to brain activity recorded from mice and monkeys engaged in identical tasks.

interventions.name: We will measure the brain networks of healthy participants using MEG/EEG while they perform naturalistic tasks in a virtual reality (VR) environment. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy people with normal or corrected-to-normal vision take part in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
The typical exclusion criteria for psychological studies apply. In particular, participants are excluded if:
o Psychological, psychiatric or neurological diagnoses or treatments, acute or in the past
o Currently taking medication (except contraceptives)
o Acute influence of alcohol or drugs
In addition, the standard exclusion criteria for MEG and MRI scans listed here apply:
o Presence of a pacemaker or neurostimulator
o Wearers of (surgical) metal implants or prostheses (including retainers - wire behind the teeth; braces; metal plates, screws, splinters; fusion pumps; aneurism clips; joint replacements, etc.)
o Non-removable dentures or braces 
o Permanent make-up 
o Tattoos 
o a metal-containing coil (intrauterine device) 
o Claustrophobia
